title: /login records when a signed-out person starts signing in (login.code_requested, login.oauth_started), with the source and never the address
steps: S1: POST /login (JSON) with an address and utm fields; with another address and no utm; with 'not-an-address'.
S2: GET /signin/google with utm fields; without; GET /signin/github on a deployment where GitHub is not configured.
S3: GET /signin/google 31 times from one client address.
expect: S1: 200, 200, 400; two login.code_requested rows with account_id null, the first {source, medium, content} cleaned, the second {}; no row holds the address.
S2: 302, 302, 404; two login.oauth_started rows, {provider: 'google', source, medium, content} and {provider: 'google'}.
S3: every answer is 302; exactly 30 login.oauth_started rows.
evidence: Issue #33: the step between a visit to /login and a first sign-in could only be read from rate_bucket rows, swept after about two days
fence: Usage never stands in the way of signing in: a start row holds no address, is capped per client address, and a failure to record it never fails the request

tests: POST /login records one login.code_requested per accepted request
sign-in starts stop being recorded at the hourly cap
